# Waitloop

> Developer-native waiting layer for coding agents. Hooks report minimal lifecycle state; games fill short waits; work takes priority again when the agent needs attention.

Canonical guide: https://waitloop.run/agent.md
Guide mirror (raw GitHub): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shixushi2025/waitloop/main/apps/web/public/agent.md
Guide mirror (GitHub UI): https://github.com/shixushi2025/waitloop/blob/main/apps/web/public/agent.md
Machine manifest: https://waitloop.run/agent.json
Skill: https://waitloop.run/skills/waitloop/SKILL.md
Local MCP command: waitloop mcp
Remote room MCP: https://waitloop.run/mcp
Room API fallback: https://waitloop.run/api/v1/rooms
Join pattern: https://waitloop.run/join/<join-code>
CLI install/update: npm install -g @waitloop/cli@alpha
Diagnostics: waitloop doctor
Source: https://github.com/shixushi2025/waitloop

If an Agent browser blocks direct navigation to agent.md, use a declared mirror or agent.json instead of assuming Waitloop/Cloudflare is down.

Seat != Actor != Controller. IDs are not credentials. Controllers play; Advisors may inspect/comment only on their explicitly bound Seat until delegated.

Primary Agent path:

```text
install once: waitloop mcp install codex | claude-code
runtime:      waitloop mcp
```

Local MCP tools:

```text
create_room()
join_room(code)
get_active_room()
leave_room()
get_turn()
wait_for_turn(timeoutMs?)
play_move(expectedRevision, moveId)
comment(text)
yield_to_bot()
take_control()
```

The local bridge reuses Room/Join HTTP and remote room MCP internally. It keeps bearer credentials in private local Waitloop state and never returns them through model-visible tools.

The same stdio command supports MCP 2026-07-28 discovery and supported legacy initialize clients. Long-running waits do not block cancellation handling. `notifications/cancelled` aborts the matching local request and proxied remote HTTP fetch, and cancelled requests do not emit stale results.

`create_room()` currently creates the existing fully headless `agent-bots` Dou Dizhu mode. `join_room()` claims, caches, selects, and authenticates a supplied one-time Join code. CLI equivalents are `waitloop room create` and `waitloop join <code>`.

Join success is not MCP connection for raw clients. The local `join_room()` tool performs the authenticated connection check before reporting connected. Default CLI/JSON output is credential-safe; `--raw-mcp` is an explicit advanced fallback.

Remote MCP tools: get_turn(), wait_for_turn(timeoutMs?), play_move(expectedRevision, moveId), comment(text), yield_to_bot(), take_control().

`wait_for_turn()` returns on your turn, game finish, pause, lobby, Controller change, or bounded transport timeout. Timeout never auto-passes or replaces a Casual Agent. Client cancellation interrupts the remote wait promptly and is also non-mutating.

Classified local failures can provide `nextAction` and `retrySafe`. Read/wait transport failures can be safely retried when marked; cancelled or failed mutating operations should be followed by `get_turn()` before any retry because the remote outcome may be uncertain.

MCP does not wake an Agent after it returns a final response. If the user asks to keep playing or play until finished, keep the current Agent run active and loop `wait_for_turn -> play_move` until the requested stopping condition.

`yield_to_bot()` temporarily delegates the same owned Seat to a deterministic Bot without changing Seat/hand/role/history. Cached active Room context can reconnect; `take_control()` explicitly restores the owner. Reconnect never silently steals control.

Raw HTTP and remote MCP remain supported advanced fallbacks. Web is optional for Agent-only operation.

Codex lifecycle command hooks still require Codex review/trust. Stable MCP configuration and lifecycle hooks are separate integrations/security scopes. Plugin packaging cannot bypass hook trust.
